title: T1529 — System Shutdown/Reboot
subtitle: Watch the attack unfold step by step, from one stolen operations account to a reboot wave.

steps.title: OF 8 - STOLEN OPS LOGON
steps.caption: The attacker signs in to OPS01, an operations workstation, with an account stolen by an infostealer. Nothing looks broken yet, but this account controls many servers. The logon comes from an unknown outside address.
steps.defender: Defender hint: Alert on admin logons to operations workstations that do not come from your VPN or jump hosts.

steps.title: OF 8 - CHECK THE POWER RIGHTS
steps.caption: The attacker runs whoami /priv and sees SeShutdownPrivilege in the list. This user right allows the account to switch machines off. Now they know they hold the power switch.
steps.defender: Defender hint: Flag privilege checks on workstations and record which user rights the caller looked for.

steps.title: OF 8 - SNEAKY DELAYED REBOOT
steps.caption: The attacker schedules a delayed reboot on APP01 with shutdown /r /t 300 and a fake maintenance reason. Windows logs event 1074 at once, but the reason text looks like normal work. The timer gives them an alibi.  ?
steps.defender: Defender hint: Treat every 1074 as a question: does the caller, time, and reason match an approved change ticket?

steps.title: OF 8 - PUSH A REBOOT WAVE
steps.caption: The attacker pushes the same command to many servers through remote execution. SQL01 and WEB01 power off one after another. Users see service errors across the whole company.
steps.defender: Defender hint: Correlate shutdown commands across hosts by the same user; one account on many hosts is an incident.

steps.title: OF 8 - SOC CONNECTS THE DOTS
steps.caption: The SIEM links events 1074, 6008, and Kernel-Power 41 to one unusual account across many hosts. It raises a single critical incident for T1529. The SOC analyst starts containment.
steps.defender: Defender hint: Build this correlation before an attack: same account, many shutdown events, short time window.

steps.title: OF 8 - CONTAIN AND RECOVER
steps.caption: The SOC isolates OPS01, blocks the stolen account, and boots the affected hosts from a known-good state. Services come back and the attacker is locked out. The lesson: alert on 1074 with unexpected callers.
steps.defender: Defender hint: Keep tested boot images and backups so recovery is a runbook, not an improvisation.
